name: Irijah
overview: Irijah was a male figure known primarily as a captain of the guard, as recorded in Jeremiah 37:13. There is no information about his tribal affiliation or additional personal details beyond his military role. His position indicates a role of authority and responsibility within the context of the biblical narrative.
namesAndTitles: The name Irijah means 'YHWH sees,' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges God's awareness and oversight. This proper name, mentioned in Jeremiah 37:13, does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries a significant meaning related to divine observation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Irijah was the father of Shelemiah, as explicitly stated in Jeremiah 37:13. Beyond this paternal relationship, there are no further family connections documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Irijah's significance in Scripture stems from his role as a captain of the guard, a position that would have involved enforcing royal or governmental authority during a turbulent period. His mention in Jeremiah 37:13 situates him within the prophetic narrative, highlighting the intersection of political and spiritual events. The reference to his son Shelemiah also suggests a familial line connected to this historical moment.
